rule: Record the true north direction and keep the orientation explicit before applying zoning.
Site selection and site characteristics are treated before building layout in classical Vastu texts.
source: Mayamata ch. 1-10; Government Sanskrit archive discussion

rule: Use an explicit measurement system and proportion schedule; never mix feet and millimetres without conversion.
Treat the central zone deliberately and avoid automatically labeling every center-space rule as a universal ancient prescription.
source: Mānasāra / Vāstu-prakaraṇa tradition; rule classification policy

rule: Entrance position must be evaluated against orientation, grid and building geometry; do not use a single universal distance rule.
source: Classical Vastu planning approach; exact prescription varies by text/tradition

rule: Kitchen, toilets, stairs and utilities should be checked as functional zones as well as Vastu zones; local code and plumbing/structure take precedence where conflict exists.
source: Modern architectural synthesis; not represented as a single ancient-text rule

rule: Structural grid, column sizes, beams, foundations and seismic detailing require engineering design and must not be inferred from Vastu alone.
